content.text:
The loader rejects three valid resolver outputs:

- `extracted_name_link`
- `trade_union_family_link`
- `statistical_and_supporting_name_link`

The resolver defines all three in [declaration_resolution.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-load-error-20261009/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution.rs:27), serializes them using snake case, and selects them from accepted component evidence in [identity.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-load-error-20261009/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:427).

Resolver output goes into `observation_resolution.parquet`. The loader reads that artifact using the same Arrow schema, but deserializes `identity_basis` into an unrestricted `String` ([declaration_loading.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-load-error-20261009/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:503)). Its separate string allowlist omits those three variants ([line 166](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-load-error-20261009/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:166)).

Consequently, a valid row with a unique funder ID and a populated identity ID fails the first condition and produces `invalid or duplicate resolved observation identity`. That message combines four checks, so it misleadingly suggests duplicate identities when the actual problem is the outdated evidence-basis allowlist.

The loader already accepts the current `funder-resolution-v3` manifest, making this an inconsistent producer/consumer contract rather than a deliberately unsupported policy version. Failure occurs during artifact validation, before database loading.

No edits made.
